summary: Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhaddanta Nārada and at Harvard University and Harvard Divinity School. He taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised Burma's Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Sara Frumento is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. As of 2026, she studied for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

A Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar, McClintock earned her PhD at Harvard (2002) and studied at Columbia, CIHTS, and Lausanne. Her teachers included Tom Tillemans. She was a professor at UW-Madison (2003) and associate professor at Emory (2026).

Sarah Aoife Richardson, a specialist in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD from the University of Toronto in 2016 under Jenny Purtle. Her other teachers included John C. Huntington, Susan L. Huntington, and Dina Bangdel.

Sarah E. Fraser works in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University (1990–1991). She was an associate professor at Northwestern University (1996) and directrice d'études at the EPHE (2000).

Sarah Harding is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (1972) and Drubpon Lama Tenpa (~1976–1980). She taught at Naropa University (~1992–2018, 2008) and was a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000).

Sarah Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar who completed an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an M.A. post there, attested in 2026.

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. In 2013, she was affiliated with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies and Wolfson College, and was an Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies fellow.
Saraju Rath is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held positions at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1943 and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He directed Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and served as Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904).

Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006) under the supervision of S. Shyamkishor Singh, also having studied under S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied for a Sinhala-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Deshapriya Gunasena (attested 2026).

Saroja Bhate is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1985–2002) and as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1999–2006).
Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He held an appointment at the University of Queensland, attested as Professor of History in 1958 and again attested in 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal was a historian who studied at Madras Christian College, Presidency College Chennai, the University of Madras, and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1951). He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Christian College. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities, and was Chancellor of the University of Delhi (1953–1962).

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua and served on the teaching staff in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

Satiranjan Sen was an Indology and Sinology scholar who studied at Peking University, founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti, and served as a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University.
